title: Prime Numbers and the Sieve
summary: What primes are, why they matter and how a 2,000-year-old trick finds them.

steps.title: What is a prime?
sentences: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
The number 1 is not a prime, and 2 is the only even prime.

steps.title: The Sieve of Eratosthenes
sentences: Circle 2 and cross out every multiple of 2.
Move to the next number that is not crossed out, 3, circle it and cross out its multiples, and keep going. The numbers left standing are primes.

steps.title: Why stop early?
sentences: You only need to sieve with primes up to the square root of the largest number.
For numbers up to 50 you only need 2, 3, 5 and 7.
Any number left after that cannot have a smaller factor.

steps.title: Why primes matter
sentences: Every whole number bigger than 1 is either a prime or can be built by multiplying primes in only one way.
That makes primes the building blocks of numbers.
Very large primes keep our online messages and bank details secret.

facts: Eratosthenes was a Greek scholar who lived about 2,200 years ago and also measured the size of the Earth.
There are infinitely many primes: Euclid proved this more than 2,000 years ago.
The largest known primes have tens of millions of digits.

quiz.q: Which of these is a prime?
Which is the only even prime?
quiz.why: Every other even number can be divided by 2.

quiz.q: The numbers left after sieving are...
quiz.why: The numbers left uncrossed are the primes.
